math/rand/v2 jitters a reconnect delay so nodes that lost the controlplane together do not re-dial in lockstep. Nothing security-relevant depends on the value: it is never a key, token, nonce, id or session material, and an attacker who could predict every node's jitter gains only the timing of a dial that is retried forever anyway. The only property needed is spread, which any PRNG gives; crypto/rand would add an error path to a timer for no gain.

systemd-resolved runs as an unprivileged user (systemd-resolve) and reads drop-ins after dropping privileges. Verified on the bench 2026-08-29: with the file at 0600 and the directory at 0700, resolved SILENTLY ignored the drop-in — the routing domains vanished from `resolvectl status` and the cluster name fell straight back to mDNS, which is precisely the failure this file exists to prevent (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#202). Tightening these modes does not harden anything; it reverts the fix with no error anywhere. 0644/0755 also matches systemd's own /etc/systemd/resolved.conf and Rasputin's existing 10-rasputin-mdns.conf. Contents are a cluster id and a LAN address — no secret.

argv-form exec.CommandContext with no shell; the binary is the literal "docker". Every argument is built by the builders in this file: compose project names (projectName(appID), a lower-cased ULID), the tile's volume name as the VALUE of a `--filter label=k=v` argument (never a free operand, so a leading `-` cannot read as an option), container ids and mount destinations parsed back out of docker's own `ps`/`inspect` output, and container-side paths path.Join'd onto that absolute destination (so `sqlite3 <src>` is never option-shaped). The one place a value enters CODE is sqlite3VacuumArgv's SQL literal, where `'` is doubled; python3BackupArgv passes both paths in argv and its program text is a constant. The inspect template is a constant — the volume name is matched in Go afterwards, not interpolated. TRIP-WIRE: a builder that interpolates a name into a template or a `sh -c` string reopens this.

argv-form exec.CommandContext of the literal "docker" binary, no shell. Every argument vector is built by the *Args builders in volumes.go from constants plus docker volume names, and every name reaching those builders has passed proto.ParseAppVolumeName — rasp_<26-char Crockford ULID>_<volume>, refused otherwise — so a name cannot begin with `-`. Names appear either as the VALUE of a `--filter volume=<name>` argument or as free operands placed after a literal `--` (volumeInspectJSONArgs, volumeRmArgs), so option parsing has already ended when they are read. The RemoveProjectVolumes path additionally refuses any name whose app id is in the api's ledger, whose com.docker.compose.project label disagrees, or that a container references. TRIP-WIRE: a builder that drops the `--`, takes a name that skipped ParseAppVolumeName, or moves to `sh -c` reopens this.

Path is filepath.Join of the agent's own restore-record directory (RestoreRecordDir(stateDir), set from RASPUTIN_STATE_DIR in main.go) with an entry name this process just listed from that directory with os.ReadDir. No component derives from the bus, a request or a volume: the records are written only by writeRestoreRecord in this file, under this agent's state dir, mode 0600. What the record NAMES (a staging path) is then trusted only by shape — its base name must carry the restore-staging prefix — and the only action on it is RemoveAll of a directory this agent created beside a volume. Covered by TestSweepRestoreStagingRemovesOnlyRecordedStagingTrees, which asserts a record naming a non-staging path is left alone along with what it names.

Every path here is composed by this package, never taken from a bus field. The volume root comes from the runtime (docker volume inspect's Mountpoint, or the mock's own directory), and every file opened under it is a path filepath.WalkDir returned from walking that root — the api sends a volume NAME (BackupStageVolumeCmd.Volume) and never a path. The staged file is filepath.Join(stagingRoot, cmd.StagingName) where StagingName has passed proto.BackupValidStagingName — the SAME predicate the write verb applies: letters, digits, - _ . only, no separator, no leading dot, no ./.. — with a `.partial-` prefix, and stagingRoot is agent-side config (storage.StagingRoot). A sqlite snapshot substitute is filepath.Join(volRoot, .rasputin-quiesce, dbRel) with dbRel a walk result. TRIP-WIRE: a verb that takes a path instead of a name, or a relaxed BackupValidStagingName, makes this row real — the shape check IS the control.

The transfer verb opens the staged tar it is about to seal: filepath.Join(s.stagingRoot, cmd.StagingName), where StagingName has passed proto.BackupValidStagingName in validateTransfer (letters, digits, - _ . only, at most 128 chars, no separator, no leading dot, no `.`/`..`) and stagingRoot is this agent's own configured root (storage.StagingRoot). Same containment as the write verb's rows above: the join cannot leave the root, and it is Lstat'd and required to be a regular file before the open. The destination URI and the credential in the same command never touch the filesystem. TRIP-WIRE: a path field on BackupTransferCmd, or a StagingName that skips the shape check, reopens this.

Marker paths are filepath.Join(markerDir, name) where markerDir is agent config (<stateDir>/quiesce-armed) and name is either a file os.ReadDir returned from that directory (SweepArmedStops) or markerName(appID), which maps every rune outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] to `_` before appending .json — so a bus-supplied app id cannot carry a separator or traverse. The bytes read back are json.Unmarshal'd into armedStop (ids and a timestamp) and used only to choose WHICH app to `compose start`; a marker that does not decode is logged and left alone. TRIP-WIRE: reading any other field out of a marker, or building the name from anything but markerName, reopens this.

The one exec seam for the whole blockdev backend. There is no shell: exec.CommandContext takes an argv slice. `name` is never caller-supplied — it comes from the tools map, populated only by exec.LookPath over the fixed requiredTools/optionalTools lists, and tool() falls back to the same literal names. Every operand that originates off-box is regex-validated first (checkDevicePath / checkPartUUID reject anything not matching ^/dev/... or a UUID, which also stops a value being read as an option), and lsblk gets an explicit `--` separator before its operand. The indirection is load-bearing rather than incidental: it is what lets blockdev_test.go assert that a REFUSED claim never reached wipefs/sfdisk/mkfs, which cannot be tested on hardware. Inlining exec.CommandContext at each of the eight call sites would produce eight copies of this same finding and delete that test.

The directory fsync that makes the marker rename durable. mountPath here is the return of mountPartition — filepath.Join(mountRoot, partUUID) with partUUID already matched against ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$, so it cannot contain a separator or traverse out of mountRoot. The handle is opened only to call Sync() and is closed immediately; no content is read from it.

readMarker's path is built by the agent, not supplied by anyone: filepath.Join(mountPath, proto.StorageMarkerFile) where the filename is a package constant and mountPath is one of three agent-controlled values — mountRoot joined with a partUUID that checkPartUUID has already matched against ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9-]{0,63}$ (no separators, so no traversal), an os.MkdirTemp directory under mountRoot, or a mount point read from the kernel's own lsblk output. No api- or operator-supplied string reaches it unvalidated. The read is bounded at 64 KiB and the bytes are only json.Unmarshal'd into StorageBackupSet, never executed or echoed.

Reads the cached bundle on startup. The path is filepath.Join(stateDir, fmt.Sprintf("catalog-%d.json", version)) where version came from strconv.Atoi of the pointer file -- the Atoi is load-bearing: a non-integer pointer is rejected before this line, so no separator or traversal sequence can reach the path. Even a hostile pointer file can only name catalog-<int>.json inside the api's own state directory, and that file is re-verified before it is read.

Reads the detached signature alongside the bundle in Apply, same provenance as the bundle path: caller-chosen, in-process, never derived from remote data. Reached only after verification has already succeeded.

Reads the downloaded bundle in Apply. The PATH is chosen by the caller inside this process (the fetcher's own temp file), never parsed out of the bundle, a URL, or any network field -- the bundle's CONTENT is attacker-influenced, its location is not. The content is treated as hostile: the signature is verified against the catalog purpose on the line above this read, before any parser sees it.

Both components of every staged path are checked at the join, in stagedPath. THE DIRECTORY is the target node's staging root, which arrives in BackupPreflightAck.StagingRoot rather than being derived here — the api derived its own until 2026-09-02 and got a different answer from the agent on every shipping image. Two controls bound it: step 1 (runValidate) refuses any target whose NodeID is not RunConfig.SelfNodeID, so the ack can only have come from the agent on THIS host, a process already running as root beside the api and with nothing to gain by steering it; and checkStagingRoot then requires an absolute path equal to filepath.Clean of itself, applied both on the way in from the ack and on the way back out of the job ledger, so a relative path, a `..`, a doubled separator or a trailing slash never reaches os.MkdirAll, CleanStaging or a file open. THE NAME is minted by this package as stagingName(generationID, kind), where the id comes from proto.BackupGenerationID (a UTC timestamp, the ULID job id's tail with every non-alphanumeric mapped out, and a scope constant), and is re-checked with proto.BackupValidStagingName — the SAME predicate the agent's write verb applies to what it is sent: one path component of [A-Za-z0-9._-], at most 128 chars, no separator, no leading dot. So the join is always a direct child of the staging root. Nothing is caller-supplied: storage.RunSpec has no path field, and POST /api/backup/runs decodes with DisallowUnknownFields so an invented one is a 400 rather than a value. TRIP-WIRE: dropping the SelfNodeID check in runValidate, or building a staged path by any route other than stagedPath, makes these rows real — those two checks ARE the control.

Path is filepath.Join of the api's own configured data/trust/mesh directories (RASPUTIN_DATA_DIR and friends, resolved once in main.go) with literal directory and file names (restore-pending, restore-applied, restore.json). No component derives from a request, the bus, or the backup disk: the restore's reads OF the disk go through backupxfer/fsat (openat, O_NOFOLLOW, fstat) and never through a path-based open. The report file read here was written by this process's own PrepareRestore, bounded to maxManifestBytes, and parsed before anything is moved.

Trust-root path is never request-derived: filepath.Join(dir, "root-ca.pem") where dir is the api's configured trust dir (RASPUTIN_TRUST_DIR, else <RASPUTIN_DATA_DIR>/trust — main.go), or a t.TempDir() in tests. Checked every caller of NewVerifier/NewDevPermissiveVerifier: main.go's wireBundleVerifier and the api/updater test fixtures; no HTTP handler constructs a Verifier. The bytes read are passed only to x509.CertPool.AppendCertsFromPEM and are never returned, logged or echoed, and a missing or unparseable file fails CLOSED (unavailable verifier, ErrTrustUnavailable on every Verify), so no path through here discloses anything or softens a check.

Bundle path is server-constructed, never request-derived. Both production callers of VerifyFile (handleUploadBundle and handlePullUpdate in updates_handlers.go) pass the tmpPath that ingestBundle created with os.CreateTemp(filepath.Join(bundleDir, ".tmp"), "ingest-*.bin") — a name the kernel and the server chose; the request supplies only the bytes written into it, never the path. Traced every caller; the remaining ones are tests passing t.TempDir() paths.

artifactsig is a library and sigPath is its parameter, so this was derived from the call sites rather than from the line. catalogsync passes MkdirTemp dir + the package constant assetSig, or filepath.Join(s.dir, fmt.Sprintf(bundleName, version))+".sig" where version is an int from strconv.Atoi — no separator can enter either. The agent CLI passes operator argv on a root shell. The agent updater passes <artifact>.sig where the artifact is stateDir/bundles/<BundleID>.rootfs and BundleID is spec.BundleSHA256, hex with no separators. Independently of provenance this read is not a disclosure primitive: it is bounded by io.LimitReader(maxSigBytes+1), the bytes are only DER-parsed as CMS, and nothing derived from them is returned or logged — errors name the path, never the content. The agent no longer relies on the api's good behaviour for that last point: UpdateInstallCmd.LocalPath and BundleID used to reach this line unvalidated, and every backend now resolves them through agent/internal/updater/bundlepath.go, which requires the id to be one safe filename component and a non-empty LocalPath to land inside the bundle store. TRIP-WIRE: void if a backend stops calling resolveBundlePath, or if a new caller of artifactsig passes a path it has not constrained.

Trust-root path is never request-derived — checked against all three production callers, not assumed: artifactsig.TrustRootPath() ($RASPUTIN_TRUST_ROOT, exported by the image's unit, else the compile-time DefaultTrustRoot); the operator's --trust-root argv in `rasputin-agent verify-artifact`; and filepath.Join(trustDir, "root-ca.pem") from api config in catalogsync.NewVerifier (api/cmd/rasputin-api/main.go). The bytes are only fed to x509.CertPool.AppendCertsFromPEM — never returned, logged or echoed — and a missing or unparseable file fails closed with ErrNoTrustRoot, so no path through here discloses anything or degrades verification to a softer check.

gosec sees `nonce := make([]byte, NonceSize)` — a zero slice — reaching a Seal call, and cannot follow the per-chunk mutation inside sealChunk, which writes the big-endian chunk counter into nonce[0:8] and the last-chunk flag into nonce[8] before every call. So the nonce is a counter, not a constant. The (key, nonce) pair is unique twice over: the content key is derived fresh for EVERY call to Seal (a new ephemeral X25519 keypair per run, hashed into the HKDF salt alongside the recipient's public key), and within one run the counter increments per chunk. This is the age/STREAM construction. Moved from api/internal/storage/seal.go unchanged (2026-09-03) so the agent seals volumes with the same code; NewSealedStream calls Seal once per member, so a member never shares a content key with anything. TRIP-WIRE: this row becomes real the moment a content key is reused across two calls to Seal — i.e. if the ephemeral keypair is ever hoisted out of the function or cached per target.

G101 matches the identifier, not a secret: CodeCredentialInvalid / CodeCredentialExpired / CodeCredentialScope are the ingest endpoint's REFUSAL CODES ("credential-invalid", "credential-expired", "credential-scope") — the strings an endpoint answers with when an upload credential is bad, carried into the agent's ack and the job feed. No credential is a constant anywhere: every upload credential is minted per member by backupxfer.Authority from a per-process crypto/rand key and expires with its TTL.
